newsitem.title: USA: Chevron says has 30 pct of Azeri block.
newsitem.headline: Chevron says has 30 pct of Azeri block.

text.p: Chevron Corp said on Friday that it has a 30 percent stake in and will operate the Absheron Block offshore Azerbaijan under a deal it signed with the Azeri state oil company SOCAR in Washington.

"Absheron, formerly known as the Tagiyev Block, lies in close proximity -- 40 kilometers southwest -- of Azerbaijan's giant Guneshli-Azeri-Chirag multi-oilfield complex, and covers an area of approximately 160 square miles (400 square kilometers)," Chevron said in a statement.
The field lies in water depths ranging from 800 feet to 2,100 feet (250 meters to 650 meters) in the southern Caspian Sea.
Exploratory drilling is expected to begin in late 1999 after Chevron conducts 3-D seismic program to expand on data collected in earlier surveys, the company said.

U.S. Vice President Al Gore and Azerbaijani President Heydar Aliyev presided over ceremonies in Washington where officials of Chevron and the Republic of Azerbaijan signed documents clearing the way for Chevron's first major oil deal in Azerbaijan.
Richard Matzke, president of Chevron Overseas Petroleum and a Chevron Corp director, and SOCAR President Natik Aliyev penned the contract.

While the Absheron deal is Chevron's first major oil venture in Azerbaijan, the company has had a presence in the northern Caspian region through Tengizchevroil, the joint venture company which operates the Tengiz oil field in Kazakstan.

Chevron has a 45 percent stake in Tengizchevroil, which currently ships more than 25,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude through Azerbaijan. The oil is brought onshore at Baku and then transported by pipeline and rail through Azerbaijan to the Georgian port of Batumi, where it is exported to world markets.
Azeri oil production peaked at about 500,000 bpd in the mid-1940s, and fell significantly after World War II, reaching around 220,000 bpd in 1992.
